title: LiteLLM, by the risk it changes
summary: An open-source gateway in front of model providers and MCP servers. Its documentation describes access control on MCP tools: when a client lists or calls tools, the gateway enforces the permissions configured for it. Written as an answer, an agent granted read tools only can read and not change.

baseline.why: The model's typical deployment, with the answers this project addresses stated as they are without it: can read and change the data in its reach.

does.text: Access control on listing and calling MCP tools.
does.quote: When a client attempts to list or call tools, LiteLLM enforces access controls based on configured permissions.

changes.why: Only if the agent's key carries an explicit grant, because an empty grant list means no restriction, and only if the agent holds no direct credential for the MCP servers.

basis.quote: When a client attempts to list or call tools, LiteLLM enforces access controls based on configured permissions.

adds_note: It sits in the request path and holds the provider keys. On rate limits, its page states that servers without an entry are uncapped.
adoption: Give every agent its own key with an explicit tool grant.
Remove the agent's direct credentials for the MCP servers.

contradictions.text: The page says access control ensures that only authorised entities can discover and use MCP tools, and also that an empty grant list means no restriction.

does_not_claim: That it was tested. Nothing was installed or run; every change rests on the documentation quoted beside it.
next: Published, and sent to the project's maintainers at the same time. If a change is wrong, or another answer should move, the case changes with the date they said so.
